conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad you’re here. I’m [Your Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my job is simply to listen and understand how things have felt for you since your baby arrived.  

Today we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS. It’s a quick, 10-question check-in that helps us see how you’ve been coping emotionally over the past seven days. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone’s safety is at risk. We’ll go at your pace, and if any question feels hard, just let me know—we can pause or reword it.  

Ready to start? Here’s the first question:  

Over the last seven days, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you happy, or has that light, joyful feeling been missing most of the time?

I used to love things like taking a walk around the block with a podcast, or even just sipping my coffee while it was still hot. Lately… it’s like the color’s been drained out of all of it. I can still do those things, but they feel flat—like I’m going through the motions. Every now and then I’ll get a tiny spark, but it fades so fast. Mostly I just feel like, “What’s the point?”
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… I mean, my partner will still make little jokes, and I try to smile for him, but it feels forced. Nothing feels genuinely funny anymore. I might sort of chuckle, but it’s like I’m watching myself from outside—like I know I should find it funny, but the laughter just doesn’t come naturally.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, no… I wake up and it’s like, “What’s today even for?” I used to get excited about little plans—maybe meeting a friend for coffee or even just a quiet shower. Now it all feels like another chore. I still do them, but it’s more because I think I should, not because I’m looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... a lot. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” When I can’t get her to nap, I keep replaying everything—maybe I didn’t swaddle tight enough, maybe I ate something that upset her. My partner tells me babies just cry, but I still feel like it’s my fault for not figuring her out.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly think, “What if she stops breathing?” or I’ll imagine her choking and picture the whole scary scene. There’s no real reason—she’s healthy, the pediatrician says everything looks great—but the thoughts just barge in. I check her chest rising all the time, even when she’s quietly asleep.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… it hits out of nowhere. My heart starts racing, I get sweaty, and I feel like I need to run out of the room—even when nothing’s happening. Sometimes it’s while I’m just sitting on the couch holding the baby. It passes after a few minutes, but in that moment I’m convinced something awful is about to happen, even if I can’t name what.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like the second I finish one thing—bottle, diaper, laundry—there are three more waiting. I’ll look around the living room and just want to sit on the floor and cry because it’s never “done.” I manage to keep us both fed and safe, but it’s like treading water; I never feel on top of anything, just barely keeping my head up.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening several nights this week. I’ll finally get her down, crawl into bed myself, and then my mind just spins—worrying I’m doing everything wrong, replaying every little cry, feeling guilty about how little joy I feel. I’ll lie there for an hour or more, drift off for a bit, then jolt awake thinking I heard her. By morning I’m exhausted before the day even starts.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… that pretty much sums up most of the week. It’s like this heavy blanket I can’t shake off. I’ll look at her little face and know I love her, but the sadness is still there in the background—this constant ache. Some afternoons I just sit in the rocker with tears leaking while she naps on me, wondering why I can’t feel the happiness everyone says I should.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A few times this week, yeah. It’s usually when everything piles up—she won’t settle, the dishes are everywhere, and I realize I skipped lunch again. I’ll put her in the crib for a second, go to the kitchen, and just start sobbing. It doesn’t last long, maybe ten minutes, but the tears come out of nowhere and once they start I can’t stop them right away.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I’ve felt overwhelmed and hopeless sometimes, but I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom she deserves.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Screening Note – Postpartum Mood/Anxiety (self-report EPDS-style items)

Main symptoms endorsed:
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, daily crying spells  
- Marked guilt/self-blame regarding infant care  
- Intrusive anxious thoughts & panic episodes without clear trigger  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance difficulties related to rumination  
- Overwhelm / sense of “treading water” with routine tasks  

Patterns:
Consistent across items 1–9; notably absent self-harm ideation (item 10 denied).  
Responses suggest moderate–severe depressive features with prominent comorbid anxiety; functional impact on sleep, self-care, and infant interaction.

Screening significance:
High index of concern for major postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety disorder.  
Absent current self-harm intent, but ongoing distress warrants prompt follow-up assessment for safety, supports, and treatment options.
